name: The Donnas
label: Lookout!
lede: Four Palo Alto thirteen-year-olds started a joke band in a garage, took the same last name, and ended up on Letterman with a Kiss cover in the catalog.

eras.title: A side project eats the main band
eras.text: Brett Anderson, Allison Robertson, Maya Ford and Torry Castellano teach themselves to play at thirteen, practicing in Castellano's garage. The joke band with the matching names outlasts the serious one.

years.big: "We started the Donnas as a joke band."
years.h: Four thirteen-year-olds form a band for a school show
years.p: Brett Anderson's line from the Grammy interview. The Donnas start in May 1993 in Palo Alto and play Palo Alto High School's Day on the Green as Ragady Anne.
years.xp:
The four were all born in 1979 and self-taught, practicing in Castellano's garage. Wikipedia lists the early names as Ragady Anne, then the Electrocutes, then the Donnas. The Electrocutes were the real band, Anderson said; the Donnas were the side band.

Her reason it kept going: "We believed in what we were doing."

years.h: Everyone is a Donna, by first initial
years.p: Donna A, Donna R, Donna F and Donna C: a Ramones-style gimmick that sticks for nearly a decade.

eras.title: Lookout! gives them a record a year
eras.text: Singles for Darin Raffaelli's Super*teem!, then three albums on Berkeley's Lookout! Records between 1998 and 2001, a week in Japan and two movie cameos before the diplomas arrive.

years.h: The first album comes out on Super*teem!
years.p: The Donnas is released by Darin Raffaelli's label and later picked up by Lookout!.
years.xp:
Raffaelli worked at a Mail Boxes Etc. and recorded the early singles there after hours. Anderson told Grammy.com they threw the equipment up on the counter: "We were just us, in that Mail Boxes Etc.: in heaven."

She also recalled the smell of the donut shop next door.

years.h: American Teenage Rock 'n' Roll Machine clocks in at 24 minutes
years.p: Ten songs recorded at Trainwreck Studios in Oakland, with the band and Romeo Voltage producing. It is their first Lookout! release.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists 32,000 US copies sold by 2005 per Nielsen SoundScan. Reviews ranged from Spin's 8/10 to Pitchfork's 6.8.

years.h: Five shows in Japan, during senior year
years.p: Anderson on landing in Japan at sixteen. A week of gigs during their senior year, set up by Pinky Aoki of the Phantom Gift.
years.xp: Anderson told Grammy.com the reception made them feel, a little bit, like what the Beatles would feel like. Wikipedia places the trip in their senior year of high school, and Lookout! signed them afterward.

years.h: The Electrocutes turn up in Drive Me Crazy
years.p: The band plays itself under its old name in the teen comedy and has songs on the Jawbreaker soundtrack.

yt: Live at Tramps, New York, July 22, 1999
years.h: Get Skintight gets bigger
years.p: Jeff and Steve McDonald of [[Redd Kross|d3a4e499-19cf-4676-8aff-4a326b47cdb2]] produce at Toast in San Francisco. The record includes a cover of Nikki Sixx's "Too Fast for Love".
years.xp: Fifteen tracks in 38 minutes. Wikipedia cites SoundScan for 58,000 US copies by 2005, and the reviews ran from Entertainment Weekly's B to The Village Voice's A-minus.

years.h: A Kiss cover on the Detroit Rock City soundtrack
years.p: The Donnas appear in the Kiss teen movie and contribute a version of "Strutter", one more tie-in in a year full of them.

eras.title: Atlantic, TRL and the Letterman couch
eras.text: A major-label deal in December 2001 moves the Donnas from club floors to late-night TV, a Modern Rock hit and the Lollapalooza main stage.

years.h: The Donnas Turn 21 ends the Lookout! run
years.p: The fourth album closes their time on the label, as the band turn twenty-one.

years.cap: The four Donnas in a 2002 press photo
years.h: Atlantic Records signs the Donnas
years.p: Wikipedia dates the major-label deal to December 2001.

years.h: Spend the Night is their first Billboard 200 entry
years.p: Jason Carmer and Robert Shimp produce the Atlantic debut, which peaks at No. 62. "Take It Off" is the single.
years.xp: Lead single "Take It Off" reached No. 17 on the Modern Rock Tracks chart and the UK top 40. Wikipedia cites 450,000 US copies sold by 2005. A 2016 Cherry Red reissue added six bonus tracks.

years.cap: Anderson, Castellano, Robertson and Ford live in Cleveland, September 2002
years.h: TRL, SNL, Leno and Letterman in one year
years.p: Four late-night and music-TV spots in 2002 for a band that had been playing for a school show nine years earlier.
years.xp: The run covers Total Request Live, Saturday Night Live, The Tonight Show and Late Show with David Letterman. Wikipedia ties the TV push to "Take It Off", which hit No. 17 on the Modern Rock Tracks chart and the UK top 40.

years.h: The Lollapalooza main stage, summer 2003
years.p: The Donnas play the main stage of the festival.

years.h: Gold Medal, and the stage names go
years.p: Butch Walker produces at a Hollywood studio in June and July 2004. The band uses real names for the first time.
years.xp: Wikipedia says Castellano's wrist surgery pushed the songs to slower tempos and the DualDisc edition was recalled over a mastering error on the CD side. The album peaked at No. 76 with 87,000 US copies by June 2007.

eras.title: On their own again
eras.text: The band leaves Atlantic by mutual agreement, starts its own label, and then a shoulder injury forces a change at the drum kit. No farewell tour follows.

years.h: Australia in February: Big Day Out and Rove Live
years.p: The band tours with the festival and plays the TV show Rove Live.

years.cap: The Donnas live in Porto Alegre, Brazil
years.h: The Donnas and Atlantic part ways
years.p: The band announces the split on May 19, 2006.
years.xp: Wikipedia quotes the band calling the decision "entirely mutual and completely amicable." The next record, Bitchin', comes out on their own label.

years.h: Bitchin' arrives on Purple Feather Records
years.p: The single "Don't Wait Up for Me" comes out in March; the album follows on September 18 on the band's own label.

years.cap: The Donnas live in Porto Alegre, Brazil
years.h: Pat Benatar and Blondie on the bill, a bad shoulder in the band
years.p: On the Call Me Invincible tour, Castellano is sidelined by shoulder tendonitis.

years.h: Castellano retires from drumming; Amy Cesari steps in
years.p: Cesari, of the Demonics, takes the kit on July 9.
years.xp: Castellano went on to study at Stanford and Harvard Law School and works as an attorney, per Wikipedia.

years.h: "Tramp" premieres, and then the band quietly stops
years.p: The Donnas play it at a private show in August while recording an eighth album. Anderson later said they wrapped up in 2012.
years.xp: Anderson told Grammy.com the group ended after seven albums with no farewell tour. In her words, "Everything grew very gradually and incrementally," and the ending went the same way.

eras.title: The records stay in print
eras.text: Reissues keep the catalog circulating while the members build other careers.

years.h: Cherry Red reissues Spend the Night with six bonus tracks
years.p: The reissue lands in November.

years.h: Anderson finishes the psychology degree she started in 1997
years.p: She works as a palliative-care social worker in Long Beach, per Grammy.com.

years.h: Record Store Day gets Early Singles 1995–1999
years.p: The April compilation gathers the pre-Atlantic singles.
